P1.evidence: Setter referenced but notes not read back: 'Kim said that you're my kind of guy, Shane.' Frame was three-part and loose — 'I want to get a good idea where you're at, really build out what it is that you want. And then we can talk about the coaching if there's alignment' — no 'what's in the way' element and no explicit 'Does that work?', though the prospect answered 'Sounds wonderful.' Open question ran verbatim: 'What were you hoping we could potentially help you with, man?'

P2.evidence: No baseline was gathered at all. Height, weight, occupation, injury history and current training were all volunteered inside one eight-minute monologue; the rep asked no data question and did not follow up on the shoulder, the knees or the diet. Age, sleep and energy never surfaced.

P3.evidence: Only goal probe was 'What does that look like, dude? The best version.' after the prospect used the phrase. No aesthetics/function question, no 'something you can't do right now', no bridge to what is really driving it, no impact-on-others question, no reflect-back. The prospect volunteered legacy material ('so I can be an example for the children') and the rep did not develop it.

P4.evidence: The prospect described a failed self-directed rebuild that injured him and a partial current solution stack, all unprompted. The rep asked nothing about what had been tried, why it did not stick, or what is structurally in the way.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame of any kind. The two-year question, the settle-for question and the line-in-the-sand were never asked, despite the prospect handing the rep a vivid cost-of-inaction narrative.

P6.evidence: No belief question and no all-in question. The rep moved straight from the monologue to 'Would you say you're in a position to invest into something like that?' — a budget check standing in for a commitment check.

P11.evidence: No offer presented and no close attempted, so payment and onboarding could not be reached.

objection_plays.detail: Prospect raised money himself ('And there's also a financial component'). The rep never isolated ('Finances aside — nothing else keeping you from 100%?'), never used the should-I/how reframe, never mentioned that some clients break payment up, and took no part of the financial picture — no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no cards, no investments. He asked one binary qualifying question and accepted the soft no.

Prospect deferred 3-6 months pending a new income stream. None of the OD moves ran — no 'things never slow down', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets' (unusually relevant given a compounding postural injury), no 'what if all you had to do was show up'. The rep endorsed the delay and pivoted to book recommendations.

Clinical-fit trigger with no scripted play: an active shoulder injury, diagnosed skeletal misalignment, knee symptoms under load and a self-inflicted re-injury from loading too fast. The playbook has no path here, and the rep neither screened it nor asked whether any clinician had cleared loaded work — he offered informal help instead.

notes: The rep built genuine rapport and then stopped selling: eight minutes of unstructured listening, several minutes of anime chat, one budget question, and a nurture close. Coach the discipline of asking baseline and goals questions even when the prospect is talkative — everything needed to run P3 through P6 was volunteered and none of it was used.
